prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” lawyer for every truck-accident case — the right attorney depends on the facts of your crash, the injuries, the at-fault truck carrier (local carrier vs. interstate trucking company), and whether you want a lawyer who will try the case in court or prefers settling it.

How to find the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for your truck accident
- Look for specific truck-accident experience: attorneys who regularly handle commercial truck liability, FMCSA rules, black-box and ELD data, cargo/maintenance records, and who work with accident-reconstruction experts.
- Trial experience and results: pick a lawyer with a record of substantial settlements or verdicts in truck cases, not only auto-fender-benders.
- Board certification and memberships: Texas Board of Legal Specialization certification in Personal Injury Trial Law (if any), membership in the Texas Trial Lawyers Association (TTLA) or American Association for Justice are helpful signals.
- Resources and team: truck cases often require costly experts (reconstruction, biomechanics, medical, economic). Make sure the firm can front those costs.
- Communication and availability: confirm who will handle the case day-to-day and how you’ll be updated.
- Fees and costs: most truck-injury lawyers work contingency (no fee unless you recover). Ask about how costs are handled if there’s no recovery.
- Reputation and ethics: check State Bar of Texas for disciplinary history and read client reviews on Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, and Google.

Immediate practical steps
- Preserve evidence: photos, dashcam/phone video, medical records, police report, witness names and contact info, truck number and carrier info, any electronic logs.
- Statute of limitations (Texas): generally two years from the date of the accident for personal injury claims — don’t wait.
- Request a few consultations: talk to 3–4 attorneys who handle truck cases and compare strategy, likely value, and willingness to go to trial.

Questions to ask during an initial consult
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases against the carrier involved in my crash (local vs. interstate)?
- What was your typical recovery range for cases like mine?
- Who will be working on my case, and how often will I get updates?
- How do you handle expert expenses? What is your contingency fee and what costs might be deducted from a recovery?
- How long do you expect my case to take?

If you want, I can:
- Find top-rated truck-accident lawyers in Dallas and give you a short list (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood).
- Help you draft an email or script for first consultations.
- Explain what documents to bring to the consult.
